rfi.title: ‘We want to stop being afraid’: thousands join anti-RN demonstration in Orléans
rfi.description: Thousands of people marched peacefully through Orléans on Saturday to protest against the far-right National Rally as the party held its congress a few kilometres away, with demonstrators calling for solidarity and voicing their concerns about 2027.

rfi.title: France protests begin largely peacefully under heavy police presence
rfi.description: Fresh demonstrations against the rising cost of living began in a largely peaceful atmosphere across France on Saturday, with protesters calling for better pay and a better future as authorities mounted a major security operation to prevent a repeat of last weekend’s violence.

rfi.title: Deadly shooting west of Paris ‘clearly terrorist’ attack, interior minister says
rfi.description: One person was killed and four others were wounded, including a 12-year-old girl, when shots were fired from a car in two suburbs west of Paris on Friday. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the shooting was “clearly a terrorist crime” and “a racist, probably Islamophobic attack”.

rfi.title: Young Israeli voters lean right, as election puts Netanyahu to the test
rfi.description: Young Israelis preparing to vote in parliamentary elections on Tuesday are leaning further to the right than their elders, with some drawn to the far right and its focus on security. In Rehovot, a city whose results tend to mirror the national vote, RFI met a generation shaped by the attacks of 7 October, 2023 and three years of war.

rfi.title: Azerbaijan hijab ban exposes strain in ‘brotherly’ ties with Turkey
rfi.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, a staunch advocate of Muslim rights, has been notably silent on Azerbaijan’s recent hijab ban in schools. For years, Erdogan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev have shared a close alliance, but the ban is putting the Turkish president in a tight spot.

rfi.title: ‘Too arrogant, too sure of itself’ France confronts its legacy in Africa
rfi.description: Fifteen years after France promised a new relationship with Africa, Paris is still struggling to reconcile its rejection of colonial-era interference with its desire to retain influence on the continent. RFI Africa specialist Christophe Boisbouvier argues in a new book that France can still build a partnership of equals – based on respect rather than arrogance or domination.

rfi.title: France mobilises 70,000 police and gendarmes for Saturday protests
rfi.description: France will deploy some 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide during a fresh round of protests this weekend, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Friday, as President Emmanuel Macron met with student organisations at the Élysée Palace for the first time since the high school protests started more than a month ago.

rfi.title: Student-led movement seeks to unseat ruling party in Serbian election
rfi.description: Serbia's student-led protest movement is mounting its biggest challenge yet to former president Aleksandar Vucic, as voters prepare to elect a new parliament on Sunday after nearly two years of demonstrations against alleged corruption.

rfi.title: Orléans tightens security ahead of far-right National Rally party congress
rfi.description: Orléans says it will impose exceptional security measures ahead of the far-right National Rally's congress this weekend, when counter-demonstrations against "racism, fascism and imperialism" could drawn up to 25,000 people.

rfi.title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
rfi.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, with many feared trapped in the rubble and accusations of dangerous building work.

rfi.title: Kenya searches for missing Ugandan contact as Ebola cases rise
rfi.description: Kenyan authorities are searching for a Ugandan national who came into contact with the country's first Ebola patient in Nairobi, as the number of confirmed cases linked to the initial cluster rises to nine.

rfi.title: International Criminal Court wins EU's Sakharov human rights prize
rfi.description: Facing US sanctions, the International Criminal Court was on Thursday awarded the European Union's top rights prize, in a show of support that risks upsetting President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: Bill to make vandals pay for damage advances in wake of France's unrest
rfi.description: France has taken a further step towards making people financially responsible for damage they cause during urban riots in the wake of last weekend's unrest, when largely peaceful demonstrations over the cost of living were marred by widespread looting and destruction of public property.

rfi.title: Nearly all coral reefs at risk of collapse by 2075, conservation body warns
rfi.description: Nearly all of the world's shallow-water coral reefs face an extremely high risk of collapse within the next 50 years due to climate change, the International Union for Conservation of Nature, the the world's authority on endangered wildlife warned on Thursday.

rfi.title: Senegal unions press on with general strike days before Youth Olympics
rfi.description: Senegal’s three-day general strike entered its second day on Thursday, with unions pressing the government to honour agreements on pay, pensions and working conditions amid a deepening economic crisis. The action comes just days before Senegal hosts the Youth Olympic Games.

rfi.title: Websites go dark as AI exposes critical security flaws worldwide
rfi.description: Governments and companies around the world shut down websites as they raced Thursday to protect themselves from hacks after artificial intelligence uncovered critical flaws in a widely used programming language called PHP.

rfi.title: Cameroon's Eseka rail disaster survivors still waiting for justice, 10 years on
rfi.description: A decade after Cameroon’s deadliest rail disaster killed 79 people and injured more than 500, survivors are still living with serious injuries, some compensation remains unpaid and an appeal against the convictions over the crash has yet to be heard. RFI spoke to survivors still living with the consequences of the disaster and to the husband of a woman whose body has never been found.

rfi.title: World set to breach 1.5C warming limit as UN warns time is running out
rfi.description: Global warming is now set to breach the 1.5C target limit set out in the 2015 Paris Agreement, after decades of insufficient climate action, the United Nations Environment Programme has warned. Temperatures could still be reduced, but only with far larger emissions cuts and the removal of vast amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere using methods the UN says are "costly and risky".

Vie chère, services publics, justice : les raisons de la colère du 24 octobre
france24fr.description: Pouvoir d’achat, éducation, services publics et justice : la mobilisation du 24 octobre rassemble des revendications multiples. Notre invité, Benjamin Ball, porte-parole de la Coordination des gilets jaunes, revient sur les raisons de la colère et les perspectives d’une convergence des luttes.

france24fr.title: Mobilisations en France : 135 interpellations en marge des manifestations du 24 octobre
france24fr.description: À la mi-journée, 135 interpellations ont été recensées en France, selon Laurent Nuñez. À Lyon, des affrontements ont opposé des manifestants aux forces de l'ordre. À Paris, en revanche, le cortège avance dans le calme, sans dégradation ni incivilité signalée. Parti de la porte d'Italie, il évolue en périphérie, tandis que le dispositif de sécurité est davantage concentré au cœur de la capitale et que la présence policière reste discrète autour de la manifestation, témoigne notre envoyé spécial L

france24fr.title: 🔴 Mobilisation du 24 octobre en direct : 110 000 personnes dans le cortège à Paris, "situation calme" selon la préfecture
🔴 Mobilisation du 24 octobre en direct : du gaz lacrymogène tiré contre les manifestants à Lyon, Lille, Toulouse et Nantes
Au Kenya, un immeuble de 18 étages en construction s'effondre, les secours mobilisés
france24fr.description: Un immeuble de plusieurs étages s'est effondré vendredi à Nairobi alors qu'il était encore en construction. De nombreuses personnes pourraient être coincées sous les décombres, tandis que les opérations de sauvetage se poursuivent. Récit d'Emily Boyle.

france24fr.title: Brésil : Lula et Bolsonaro s’affrontent dans un ultime débat tendu à la veille du scrutin
france24fr.description: À J-1 de la présidentielle brésilienne, Lula et Jair Bolsonaro se sont retrouvés pour un dernier face-à-face sans concession. Économie, santé et retraites ont rythmé les échanges, ponctués de tensions et d’attaques personnelles. Récit d'Ethan Hajji.

france24fr.title: Une forte mobilisation anti-Rassemblement National à Orléans en marge du congrès du parti
france24fr.description: "On s’unit pour montrer qu’on est contre" : depuis ce matin, les manifestants défilent à Orléans contre le Rassemblement national, qui tient son congrès dans la ville. Associations, syndicats et partis politiques ont appelé à cette mobilisation. Le rassemblement se déroule dans le calme, mais les autorités redoutent des débordements en marge du congrès. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: L’armée israélienne mène une vaste opération en Cisjordanie après la mort de deux soldats
france24fr.description: Deux soldats israéliens ont été tués vendredi dans une attaque en Cisjordanie. Quelques heures plus tard, l’armée israélienne a lancé une opération massive, au cours de laquelle des bulldozers ont détruit des constructions palestiniennes jugées illégales par les autorités israéliennes. Récit d'Alice Brogat.

france24fr.title: Jordan Bardella, réélu président du Rassemblement national avec 98,98 % des voix
france24fr.description: Plus de 76 000 militants étaient rassemblés, samedi, à Orléans pour le congrès du Rassemblement national. Seul candidat, Jordan Bardella a été réélu président de la formation d'extrême droite avec 98,98 % des voix.

france24fr.title: "Femmes extrêmes" : trois visages féminins de la poussée de l’extrême droite en Europe
france24fr.description: Invitée d’Au cœur de l’info, Marion Van Renterghem présente « Femmes extrêmes », consacré à Marine Le Pen, Giorgia Meloni et Alice Weidel. Comment ces dirigeantes incarnent-elles les colères qui traversent les sociétés européennes ? Et quelle place le sentiment de désordre occupe-t-il dans la stratégie de Marine Le Pen ?

france24fr.title: Les commerçants parisiens dans l'inquiétude face à la mobilisation du 24 octobre
france24fr.description: "Gilets jaunes", syndicats, lycéens et étudiants sont dans la rue ce 24 octobre. À Paris, de nombreux commerçants ont choisi d'ouvrir malgré les craintes de dégradations et les inquiétudes pour leurs commerces et leurs salariés. Pour en parler, notre invité est Thierry Véron, président de la Fédération des commerçants et artisans parisiens.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation du 24 octobre : le cortège parisien défile sur un parcours qui fait débat
france24fr.description: Parti de la porte d’Italie à l’appel de l’intersyndicale, le cortège parisien avance dans une ambiance bon enfant, sans incident signalé. Mais le parcours, proche du périphérique et différent de celui demandé par les syndicats pour des raisons de sécurité, suscite des réactions parmi les manifestants. Ludovic de Foucaud, envoyé spécial de France 24, décrit l’ambiance sur place.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : 1 200 Palestiniens déplacés par l'armée israélienne à Hébron après une attaque
france24fr.description: À quelques jours d'élections législatives s'annonçant serrées en Israël, Benjamin Netanyahu a ordonné une opération militaire majeure en Cisjordanie. Entre 150 et 250 familles ont été chassées de leurs maisons, dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi, à Hébron, plus grande ville du territoire palestinien occupé depuis 1967.

france24fr.title: Mobilisations en France : jusqu'où peut-on restreindre le droit de manifester ?
france24fr.description: En France, plusieurs manifestations du 24 octobre ont été interdites ou restreintes. Dans quelles circonstances les autorités peuvent-elles légalement limiter le droit de manifester ? Réponse avec notre invité Maître Moret Bailly, professeur agrégé des facultés de droit et avocat au barreau de Paris.

france24fr.title: À Orléans, forte mobilisation anti-RN face au congrès du parti
france24fr.description: À Orléans, des militants venus s'opposer au congrès du Rassemblement national, organisé au Zénith, se rassemblent dans un village antifasciste placé sous haute surveillance. Deux périmètres de sécurité distincts ont été mis en place pour séparer les rassemblements. Une scène a également été installée pour les prises de parole, avec notamment l'intervention du maire de Trappes, qui a dénoncé des "discours de haine" qui "tuent et font des victimes". Le point sur la situation avec notre envoyée spé

france24fr.title: Mobilisation du 24 octobre : le cortège parisien change de parcours
france24fr.description: À Paris, le cortège s'apprête à démarrer sur un parcours alternatif accepté par l'intersyndicale, mais dont tous les manifestants n'ont pas été informés. Parmi les slogans, certains défendent le droit de manifester. Ludovic de Foucaud, envoyé spécial de France 24, fait le point en direct du cortège parisien.

france24fr.title: Les Israéliens expatriés face au voyage du retour pour voter aux législatives
france24fr.description: À l’approche des élections législatives du 27 octobre en Israël, de nombreux expatriés comptent peser sur le scrutin. Mais pour voter, ils doivent rentrer au pays : ni vote par correspondance ni procuration ne leur permettent de participer depuis l’étranger. Reportage de David Gilberg.

zeit.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Frankfurter Sportchef-Suche - Hellmann: Gibt drei Kandidaten
Proteste in Frankreich: Mehrere Hunderttausend Menschen gehen in Frankreich auf die Straße
zeit.description: Die Proteste in Paris blieben ​weitgehend friedlich. In anderen Städten kam es zu gewaltvollen Auseinandersetzungen. Die Gelbwesten kündigen bereits weitere Proteste an.

zeit.title: Literaturpreis: Autorin Wunnicke mit Georg-Büchner-Preis ausgezeichnet
Einsatz von Tränengas: 410.000 Menschen nehmen an Protesten in Frankreich teil
Bundesliga, 7.Spieltag - Samstag: Bremen schlägt Mainz, schwerer Zusammenstoß bei Kopfball in Köln
zeit.description: Niclas Füllkrug verhilft Bremen mit zwei Elfmetern zum Sieg gegen Mainz. Robin Gosens und Soufiane El-Faouzi verletzten sich bei einem Zusammenstoß. Die Spielberichte

zeit.title: B29 wieder frei: Motor fliegt 50 Meter weit - Auto bei Unfall zerlegt
Handwerk: Kfz-Techniker ist bester Meister Sachsen-Anhalts
Westjordanland: Rund 1.500 Palästinenser aus Wohngebieten in Hebron vertrieben
zeit.description: Bei der Großoffensive im Westjordanland hat das israelische Militär Menschen aus Vierteln in Hebron vertrieben. Örtliche Medien berichten von rund 1.500 Betroffenen.

zeit.title: Turn-WM in Rotterdam: «Krass»: Kevric gewinnt WM-Silber - Nemour in eigener Liga
Julia Malik: Sie dachte, sie kriegt das allein hin. Niemand kriegt das allein hin
zeit.description: Sie träumte von einem Leben mit dem Mann. Stattdessen landete sie wegen ihm im Krankenhaus. Schauspielerin Julia Malik spricht erstmals über die Gewalt, die sie erlebte.

zeit.title: Krieg in der Ukraine: Selenskyj bestätigt Aufhebung der Starlink-Beschränkungen
zeit.description: In einem Video erklärt Wolodymyr Selenskyj die Starlink-Verbindungen des ukrainischen Militärs für wiederhergestellt. Der Präsident dankte dafür auch Donald Trump.

zeit.title: »Game on Symphony«: Wenn Beethoven zum Endgegner wird
zeit.description: Ein Symphonieorchester spielt Melodien aus »Final Fantasy« und »Resident Evil«. Hier muss die Musik ohne die Videospielwelten auskommen, für die sie geschrieben wurde.

zeit.title: Ofenkürbis mit Risottofüllung und Grünkohlsalat: Kürbis ohne Schrecken
zeit.description: Im Oktober werden Kürbisse ausgehöhlt, wir füllen statt Kerzen lieber Reis hinein. Dazu ein Salat, der sich Superfood nennen darf, vor allem aber verdammt lecker ist.

zeit.title: Landesparteitag: Dorothee von Hoff ist neue FDP-Vorsitzende in Thüringen
Blutdruckforschung: »Meine Bürotür war immer offen, es gab Flens und Rotwein«
zeit.description: Detlev Ganten hat die Blutdruckforschung revolutioniert. Nach 25 Jahren im Labor wechselte er ins Management – und rettete nach dem Untergang der DDR die Charité.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Starlink läuft laut Selenski wieder stabil +++ Melania Trump vermittelt Waffenruhe in besetzter Frontstadt Oleschki
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Wegen Demonstrationen: Die Polizei begleitet den Parteitag des Rassemblement national in Orléans mit einem Grossaufgebot
nzz.description: Ausgerechnet am ersten Wochenende nach den grossen Krawallen in Frankreich hat Marine Le Pen ihren ersten grossen Auftritt im Präsidentschaftswahlkampf. Von der derzeitigen Stimmungslage im Land dürfte sie profitieren.

nzz.title: Hitlers «Teehaus» am Obersalzberg brennt nieder: Der mutmassliche Brandstifter ist laut der Staatsanwaltschaft psychisch krank
nzz.description: Die Berggaststätte Kehlsteinhaus hoch über Berchtesgaden ging in der Nacht auf Samstag in Flammen auf. Die Polizei hat eine verdächtige Person festgenommen. Die Ruine soll wieder aufgebaut werden.

nzz.title: Weltcup-Auftakt: Der Premierensieg von Paula Moltzan, der gelungene Start der Camille Rast und das Zeichen von Emma Aicher
nzz.description: Die Amerikanerin Paula Moltzan gewinnt das Rennen in Sölden hauchdünn vor Lara Colturi. Die Deutsche Emma Aicher fährt erstmals auf das Riesenslalom-Podest. Beste Schweizerin ist Camille Rast auf dem sechsten Rang.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Proteste in Frankreich: Die Polizei nimmt 135 Personen fest – Demonstration in Orléans gegen das Rassemblement national
nzz.description: Seit Ende September gehen Schüler, Lehrpersonen und Gewerkschaften auf die Strasse – und lösen eine landesweite Bewegung aus, die zu Krawallen und Gewalt führt. Die neusten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: Vincent Kompany fällt nach seinem Kollaps wohl für mehrere Wochen aus: Was bedeutet das für Bayern?
nzz.description: Vincent Kompany hat offenbar Warnsignale seines Körpers ignoriert. Der Zusammenbruch hat Auswirkungen auf den FC Bayern.

nzz.title: Macron spricht von einem «terroristischen und rassistischen Angriff»: mindestens ein Toter und fünf Verletzte nach Schüssen im Grossraum Paris
nzz.description: Unter den Verletzten ist auch ein zwölfjähriges Kind. Die Polizei hat den mutmasslichen Täter festgenommen.

nzz.title: Verfolgungsjagd im All: Russischer Militärsatellit riskiert eine Kollision mit einem US-Satelliten
nzz.description: Wochenlang verändert ein russischer Militärsatellit seinen Kurs, bis er einem amerikanischen Radarsatelliten gefährlich nahe kommt. War die Annäherung gezielt? Die NZZ hat das Manöver anhand der Flugbahnen rekonstruiert.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Lage im Gazastreifen: Israels Armee startet Einsatz im Westjordanland
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist instabil, die humanitäre Not im Gazastreifen ist gross. Der Friedensplan der USA wurde bisher nur teilweise umgesetzt. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Müssen Grosseltern vor einer Umarmung die Zustimmung der Enkel einholen? Eine Videokampagne erregt Irland
nzz.description: Eine staatlich geförderte Organisation hat mit einem Aufklärungsfilm eine Debatte über die Grenzen der grosselterlichen Zuneigung ausgelöst. Politiker zeigen sich empört. Doch es gibt auch Gegenstimmen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Bundesratswahl: Mit einer Flut von Last-Minute-Kandidaturen lenkt die SVP von ihren Problemen ab
nzz.description: Auf einmal hat die SVP bei der Suche nach einem Nachfolger für Guy Parmelin die Qual der Wahl. Die Partei zeigt sich in ihrer ganzen Breite, doch drängt sich kein Kandidat zwingend auf.

nzz.title: Zu wenig neue Wohnungen: Das liege auch am Iran-Krieg, sagt Sika-Chef Thomas Hasler
nzz.description: Aufatmen bei einem der grössten Schweizer Industriekonzerne: Sika hat die Wende geschafft und wächst aus eigener Kraft. Aber in der Bauwirtschaft tun sich immer neue Probleme auf.

nzz.title: Wie funktioniert «bilingue» in Freiburg? Der Kanton legt erstmals Regeln für zweisprachige Gemeinden fest
nzz.description: Das Parlament hat ein Gesetz über die Amtssprachen verabschiedet. Es ist aber vor allem für die Stadt Freiburg gedacht.

nzz.title: Selbständige statt Angestellte: Just Eat stellt das soziale Versprechen der Migros auf die Probe
nzz.description: Der Essenslieferdienst Just Eat galt als Vorzeigearbeitgeber in der Branche – und kam so zu einer Partnerschaft mit der Migros. Nun kopiert Just Eat das umstrittene Modell des Konkurrenten Uber.

nzz.title: Im Clásico zwischen Barcelona und Real Madrid spielt Spanien für die Katalanen
nzz.description: Im Spitzenkampf zwischen dem FC Barcelona und Real Madrid treffen auch zwei Klubmodelle aufeinander. Barça könnte eine ganze Mannschaft mit Eigengewächsen aufstellen, Real verdient mit der Ausbildung von Fussballern das Geld für auswärtige Stars.

spiegel.title: Von Indien über Chile und die USA: Reisen mit Rollstuhl
spiegel.description: SPIEGEL-Leser Peter Hiedl sitzt im Rollstuhl, seitdem er sechs Jahre alt ist. Mit seiner Partnerin Sabine Hiedl bereiste er die Welt.

spiegel.title: Jordan Bardella als Chef des Rassemblement National wiedergewählt
spiegel.description: Er gilt als politischer Ziehsohn von Marine Le Pen: Der französische Politiker Jordan Bardella ist mit überwältigender Mehrheit im Vorsitz des rechtsnationalen RN bestätigt worden. Vor dem Parteitag gab es Proteste.

spiegel.title: »Gnade vor Recht« von Peter Grainger: Die unwahrscheinlichste Krimi-Sensation des Jahres
spiegel.description: Peter Grainger veröffentlichte seine Bestseller bisher im Selbstverlag, doch jetzt kommen sie ganz groß raus – auch in Deutschland. Dabei passiert in den leisen Krimis des Briten wenig Spektakuläres. Das macht sie aus.

spiegel.title: Winterzeit: In der kommenden Nacht werden die Uhren umgestellt
spiegel.description: Eine Stunde mehr Schlaf, aber abends wird es dafür jetzt früher dunkel: In der Nacht auf Sonntag werden die Uhren wieder auf die Normalzeit gestellt, auch Winterzeit genannt.

spiegel.title: Israel: Sonst geht es bei Wahlen um Zukunft. In Sderot wird sie von der Vergangenheit verdrängt
spiegel.description: Der Terrorangriff vom 7. Oktober ist das wichtigste Thema bei den Wahlen in Israel. Wie geht es Menschen, die persönlich betroffen sind? Ein Besuch in der Stadt Sderot, die unter Beschuss geriet, und nun politisch immer weiter nach rechts rückt.

spiegel.title: Turn-WM in Rotterdam: Helen Kevric gewinnt Silber am Stufenbarren
spiegel.description: Es ist der größte Erfolg in der Karriere von Helen Kevric: Nach ihrem EM-Titel hat die Deutsche sich nun auch bei der Weltmeisterschaft eine Medaille an ihrem Lieblingsgerät erturnt.

spiegel.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Viele Verletzte, wenige Tore – aber Werder Bremen gewinnt in Mainz
spiegel.description: Ein Bundesligaspieltag, der eher seine hässliche Seite gezeigt hat: Mehrere üble Verletzungen prägten das Bild. Aber es gab auch Positivschlagzeilen: Für die sorgte wieder einmal Werder Bremen.

spiegel.title: Mietmarkt: Warum Wohnungstausch die Wohnungsnot nicht lindert
spiegel.description: Die Immobiliensuchen sind voll davon: Immer mehr Wohnungen werden im Gegenhandel angeboten. Was für die einen eine Chance ist, lässt andere außen vor. Die Not auf dem Mietmarkt mindert der Trend ohnehin nicht.

spiegel.title: Volker Schlöndorff hört auch mit 87 nicht mit dem Filmemachen auf - warum?
spiegel.description: Seit mehr als einem halben Jahrhundert ist Volker Schlöndorff Regisseur, mit der »Blechtrommel« gewann er einen Oscar. Begegnungen mit einem, der die deutsche Filmgeschichte verkörpert wie kein anderer.

spiegel.title: Abschiebungen: Hunderte demonstrieren an Flughäfen in Deutschland
spiegel.description: In Leipzig, Frankfurt und Berlin versammelten sich Menschen, um gegen Abschiebehaft und Abschiebeflüge zu protestieren. Sie kritisieren die Kooperation der Bundesregierung mit den Taliban.

spiegel.title: CSU-Parteitag: Friedrich Merz hat zwei Bussis für Ilse Aigner dabei – mehr nicht
spiegel.description: Auf dem CSU-Parteitag schweigt der CDU-Chef zu den Ambitionen der Schwesterpartei, künftig die Bundespräsidentin zu stellen. Unmut darüber war aber nur auf den Gängen zu vernehmen.

spiegel.title: Johann Lafer beantwortet Ihre Fragen zum Kochen – neue SPIEGEL-Kolumne
spiegel.description: Ab sofort tagt das SPIEGEL-Küchenkabinett: Foodautorin Stefanie Hiekmann, Journalist Mohamed Amjahid und Starkoch Johann Lafer beantworten alle kulinarische Fragen – jeweils aus ganz eigener Perspektive.

spiegel.title: Westjordanland: Palästinenser fordern internationalen Druck nach israelischem Armeeeinsatz
spiegel.description: Nach dem tödlichen Angriff auf zwei israelische Soldaten hat Israel in Hebron umfangreiche Antiterroreinsätze gestartet. Die Palästinensische Autonomiebehörde ruft um Hilfe.

spiegel.title: Hitlers »Eagle's Nest« am Obersalzberg: Kehlsteinhaus fast vollständig zerstört – Polizei geht von Brandstiftung aus
spiegel.description: Das von den Nazis errichtete Kehlsteinhaus ist offenbar absichtlich in Brand gesetzt worden. Ein Verdächtiger wurde verhaftet, ist aber verletzt. Bayerns Innenminister will das Gebäude wiederaufbauen lassen.

spiegel.title: Proteste in Frankreich, Spanien, Italien: »Die großen Parteien müssen Rücksicht auf Rentner nehmen – also wendet sich die Jugend extremen Parteien zu«
spiegel.description: In Frankreich, Spanien, Italien und vielen weiteren EU-Ländern geht die Jugend auf die Straße. Politökonom Tim Vlandas erklärt, warum er sie versteht – und woher die Wut kommt.

spiegel.title: Islamistischer Terror: 21-jähriger Deutscher soll IS-Ausbildung geplant haben
spiegel.description: Ein junger Deutscher wollte sich mutmaßlich in Somalia und Pakistan dem IS anschließen. Jetzt wurde er nach Deutschland ausgeliefert. Was die Bundesanwaltschaft ihm vorwirft.

spiegel.title: Weltcup-Riesenslalom in Gröden: Emma Aicher ist schon im Oktober in starker Winterform
spiegel.description: Traditionell beginnt der Skiwinter im Oktober in Sölden. Emma Aicher hat offenbar im Sommer eifrig Riesenslalom trainiert – so gut wie zum Weltcup-Auftakt war sie in dieser Disziplin noch nie.

spiegel.title: Wahlkampf in Spanien: KI-generiertes Video von Frau des Premiers sorgt für Aufruhr in Spanien
spiegel.description: Im spanischen Wahlkampf hat die Opposition ein KI-generiertes Video veröffentlicht, in dem Personen aus dem Umfeld des Ministerpräsidenten angeblich Fehlverhalten eingestehen. Die Angegriffenen wehren sich.

observador.title: Nycole recusou ficar à sombra da equipa dos chapéus
observador.description: Ana Dias inaugurou marcador com um grande chapéu mas Benfica deu a volta ainda na primeira parte com bis de Nycole e praticamente resolveu dérbi antes do intervalo para saltar para a liderança (4-1).

observador.title: 17h. Habitação. Milhares de manifestantes em Lisboa e Porto
observador.description: Vários políticos marcam presença nas manifestações em Lisboa. Ainda, em França, mais de 130 pessoas foram detidas nos protestos.

observador.title: Mais de 130 pessoas detidas nos protestos em França
observador.description: O ministro francês do Interior, Laurent Nuñez, indicou que, entre as 136 ações registadas, não foi reportado qualquer incidente grave.

observador.title: Milhares de manifestantes marcharam em Madrid pelas reformas
observador.description: Multidão percorreu, de forma pacífica, quase dois quilómetros entre a estação de Atocha e a rua Alcalá, passando pelo famoso Museu do Prado e pela praça de Cibeles.

observador.title: Coletes amarelos convocam protestos para próximo sábado
observador.description: O Presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, determinou esta semana que apenas os sindicatos estavam autorizados a convocar protestos, não reconhecendo aos coletes amarelos "qualquer legitimidade".

observador.title: 16h. Organização estima 25 mil manifestantes em Lisboa
observador.description: A PSP tem um dispositivo policial preparado para acompanhar as manifestações pelo direito à habitação em várias cidades do país. Ainda, o Irão pode estar a ampliar os planos de ataque.

observador.title: Aquilo que tem mesmo de saber sobre o Estripador de Lisboa
observador.description: Agora que o Podcast Plus do Observador deu origem a uma peça de teatro imersivo, contamos o que tem mesmo de saber sobre os crimes e a investigação ao Estripador de Lisboa.

observador.title: PSP promete privilegiar o diálogo com os manifestantes
observador.description: Polícia de Segurança Pública garante que terá uma "lógica de prevenção e de gestão proporcional de eventuais ocorrências".

observador.title: O negociador que libertou um refém por mil palestinianos
observador.description: A negociação com o Hamas para libertar o soldado Shalit em 2011. Uma espera a Witkoff na casa de banho. E o apelo a Trump: “Tem de dizer a Netanyahu: ‘Termina com isto!’” Entrevista a Gershon Baskin.

observador.title: PSP atenta a apelos nas redes para atacar manifestantes
observador.description: PSP está a avaliar apelos ao ataque às manifestações pelo direito à habitação deste sábado. Autoridades estão a fazer "diligências" para evitar incidentes que perturbem o direito à manifestação.

observador.title: 15h. Habitação. Arranca a esta hora um protesto em Lisboa
observador.description: Os protestos pela habitação vão acontecer um pouco por todo o país. Ainda, Luís Neves garante que não há braço de ferro com os manifestantes.

observador.title: Não começou o desconto mas já estão a descontar: City perde
observador.description: Numa fase em que se fala cada vez mais na hipótese de descida ao Championship pela dedução de pontos, City não conseguiu prolongar série de sete vitórias e perdeu em Birmingham com Aston Villa (2-1).

observador.title: 14h. MAI garante que não há braço de ferro com manifestantes
observador.description: Luís Neves diz que o tema da habitação é legítimo e acredita que os protestos de hoje vão ser "ordeiros e pacíficos". Ainda, antigo presidente da AR defende um bloco central para combater o Chega.

observador.title: Cotrim falha reeleição como vice da bancada dos liberais
observador.description: Portugal tinha vice-presidências nos três maiores grupos do Parlamento Europeu e passa a ter apenas uma. Manobra de macronistas trama Cotrim, que passa de segundo mais votado a ficar fora do top 8.

observador.title: 13h. Base das Lajes. 17 aviões dos EUA estacionados
observador.description: Durante a manhã, nenhum levantou voo. Ainda, MAI garante que não há braço de ferro com os manifestantes.

observador.title: Jornada ao rubro: discurso afiado e duelos de fogo em campo
observador.description: A 9.ª jornada traz os três grandes perante as surpresas da época. Do ambiente no Dragão às novidades na Luz, este fim de semana promete ser de puro entretenimento e grande emoção até ao último minuto.

observador.title: 12h. Habitação. IL mais preocupada com a inação do governo
"Só o consenso multipartidário traz estabilidade ao mercado"
observador.description: Filipa Roseta, ex-vereadora da Habitação da CML, defende que a crise só se resolve com um consenso multipartidário e a criação de um mercado de habitação verdadeiramente acessível.

phys-org.title: Newly identified protein pathway helps HIV stay hidden despite treatment
phys-org.description: Current HIV medicines are effective at suppressing the virus in the blood. However, HIV can remain "asleep" or dormant inside certain immune cells and in the brain. These hidden pockets of virus, called HIV reservoirs, are the main reason HIV cannot be cured with today's treatments.

phys-org.title: Nanoscale alloy redesign tackles cold brittleness for potential deep-space and deep-sea applications
phys-org.description: Metallic materials used in extremely cold environments must maintain high strength, ductility and fracture toughness to support applications in aerospace, clean energy, superconducting systems and deep-space exploration. However, traditional alloys often suffer performance degradation at ultralow temperatures because of the long-standing trade-off between strength, ductility and toughness. Although metals may become stronger at lower temperatures, they can also become more brittle and prone to f

phys-org.title: Seabird family tree predicts which species accumulate plastic better than diet, global analysis finds
phys-org.description: What seabirds eat might seem like a good starting point for identifying species that tend to accumulate plastic in their digestive systems. Yet a recent global analysis suggests that mapping the evolutionary relatives of birds could offer better clues than their diets or feeding methods alone.

phys-org.title: Ancient stalagmites reveal exceptions to Asia–South America monsoon seesaw over the past 450,000 years
phys-org.description: In places like South Asia, Africa and parts of the Americas, monsoon rains supply water for drinking, crops and hydropower for billions of people. Understanding the patterns that monsoons tend to follow can help people plan for drought risks affecting agriculture, reservoirs and hydropower across distant regions.

phys-org.title: Cleaner brick kilns cut pollution, but gains did not reach workers, research finds
phys-org.description: Relatively simple changes to the way traditional brick kilns operate in Bangladesh can reduce pollution, save fuel and improve the quality of bricks they produce.

phys-org.title: New long‑clawed British dinosaur is the first of its kind in Europe
phys-org.description: The fossilized skull of a new species of mysterious meat-eating dinosaur from the Isle of Wight has been rediscovered in the collections of the Natural History Museum after over 100 years in storage.

phys-org.title: Swinging virtual lightsabers and punching improve pattern-based learning in VR tests
phys-org.description: Punching a virtual response box or swinging a virtual lightsaber can dramatically improve learning on certain tasks, according to new research from Florida Atlantic University's College of Engineering and Computer Science, which challenges long-standing assumptions about how people learn.

phys-org.title: Typhoon Champi knocks out power to thousands in Taiwan
phys-org.description: Emergency crews scrambled on Saturday to restore power to tens of thousands of homes in Taiwan after Typhoon Champi's fierce winds battered the island, with the storm moving toward China and Japan.

phys-org.title: NASA adopting Apollo's urgency to build a moon base and land astronauts within 2 years
phys-org.description: NASA is moving fast on its plans to build a moon base and return astronauts to the lunar surface in as little as two years.

phys-org.title: Surveying the genetic battlefield to uncover the rules of rapid evolution
phys-org.description: The Malik Lab thrives on competition. But for HHMI investigator Harmit Malik and his team at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, it's the genomes—not the people—that are in conflict. The lab studies rapid evolution—the genetic changes that happen in a species over a few generations rather than thousands of years. These fast changes are often fueled by genetic conflicts—competitions between different entities trying to maximize their success at the expense of another.

phys-org.title: Child-led citizen science helps Ecuadorian community tackle beach pollution and shape environmental decisions
phys-org.description: Pollution from human-generated waste in marine ecosystems has reached critical levels, with cigarette butts (CBs) among the most persistent and harmful pollutants. Globally, an estimated 4.5 trillion cigarette butts are discarded annually, making them the most common type of litter on beaches over the past three decades.

phys-org.title: Habitat explains Finnish animal distributions better than climate, study finds
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Helsinki wanted to understand which is the dominant factor for species occurrence and abundance: the climate or habitat-related variables, such as their natural state and the share of land shaped by human activity. Solutions to mitigate biodiversity loss depend on the answer to this question.

phys-org.title: Power cuts and sleep: Students link load shedding to anxiety, disrupted rest and lower grades
phys-org.description: South Africa endured its worst year of load shedding (scheduled power cuts by the country's utility, Eskom) in 2023. The power went off on 335 of the year's 365 days, often several times a day. Since then, the country has gone more than a year and a half without these planned power cuts.

phys-org.title: Glowing plants reveal immune responses around infection sites via two colors
phys-org.description: Researchers at the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences (LMS) have developed a new way to make glowing biological reporters more accurate, allowing scientists to track gene activity in living plants over days, weeks and potentially even months and years. The approach could help researchers study how plants respond to disease, pests and environmental stress, while opening the door to similar applications in animal and human disease models.

phys-org.title: Study maps the human side of flood risk
phys-org.description: When heavy rain hits a city, knowing where water will accumulate is only part of the picture. Who lives in the affected buildings? How might flooding disrupt their lives? And where could additional support make the greatest difference?

phys-org.title: Counting magnetic flux quanta offers new way to measure photon numbers
phys-org.description: Researchers at AIST have directly observed magnetic flux quanta generated in a superconductor by photon absorption and demonstrated a new principle of photon detection that identifies the number of photons based on the number of these flux quanta.

phys-org.title: 'It's pretty toxic… but just a little, I want to be like that': What young men think of manosphere content
phys-org.description: Masculinity content promises young men self-optimization and success, but often delivers health harms, risk-taking, unattainable standards, gender stereotypes and misogyny. The latter is the strongest predictor of violent extremism.

phys-org.title: Scientists demonstrate AI-designed enzyme for drug synthesis
phys-org.description: The new RFD4-Proteina unified generative model for protein design—created by the Institute for Protein Design (IPD) in collaboration with NVIDIA—uses advanced AI to generate entirely new protein sequences and structures, achieving computational design success rates five to 10 times higher than previous models and generating candidates five to 10 times faster.

undark.title: Podcast: The Entanglements Series Finale
undark.description: Welcome to the last installment of Entanglements, at least for the foreseeable future. In this final episode, hosts Brooke Borel and Anna Rothschild are joined by Undark editor-in-chief Tom Zeller Jr. to talk about the show’s successes, failures, and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Michael Geruso, an associate professor of economics at the University of Texas at Austin, and Jennifer Dowd, a professor of demography and population health at the University of Oxford, about population trends and fertility rates.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

While Europe has much to do to improve its external competitiveness, it must not ac

proj-syn.title: Who Pays the Fiscal Watchdogs?
proj-syn.description: Civil-society oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance, because it enables independent scrutiny long before a default. But given that a borrowing government will never volunteer to fund the people who audit it, global decision-makers must do so using agreements for stolen-asset recovery and sovereign-debt treatments.

proj-syn.title: How to Help Left-Behind Regions
proj-syn.description: Pouring public investment into poorer towns and cities might be politically beneficial, but the economic returns of indiscriminate largesse would be limited. A better approach would concentrate investment in areas with the potential to become high-productivity hubs, such as large peripheral cities.

proj-syn.title: The Agentic Information Economy
proj-syn.description: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

proj-syn.title: A Competitive Europe Must Be Climate-Resilient
proj-syn.description: Extreme weather and climate-related events caused €822 billion in economic losses across the European Union between 1980 and 2024, with a quarter of the losses occurring just in the last five years. The consequences for Europe’s competitiveness and economic security are clear—and so is the appropriate response.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Prepare for the Worst
proj-syn.description: Those seeking to weaken the EU’s supranational foundations are already preparing their radical schemes, like the “new deal for Europe” that Germany's Alternative für Deutschland recently presented in the European Parliament. The pro-EU camp must be prepared with new political strategies and institutional arrangements.

proj-syn.title: Nature Can’t Wait
proj-syn.description: Although the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine are spurring governments to increase spending on defense and focus more on economic growth, it would be a mistake to postpone investments designed to protect nature. In fact, meeting internationally agreed targets could add up to $450 billion to annual global GDP by 2050.

proj-syn.title: Argentina’s Economic Chainsaw Massacre
proj-syn.description: Argentine President Javier Milei may currently be a lynchpin in US President Donald Trump’s geoeconomic vision for Latin America; but he could soon become its weak link. With elections coming next year, he has achieved an economic recovery and relative price stability by driving millions of his people into destitution.

proj-syn.title: Which AI Myth Will We Embrace?
proj-syn.description: The mythos—or foundational stories—that we tell ourselves will determine our fate in the age of AI. As industry leaders regale us with utopian visions of benevolent digital gods delivering scientific breakthroughs and expanding our technological horizons, our best defense against hubris is a counternarrative of social cooperation.

proj-syn.title: No More Superpowers
proj-syn.description: Although the United States remains very powerful and Russia still commands enormous conventional and nuclear capabilities, each country’s global status has come to be defined by failure and constraint. If anything, both may belong to the same broad grouping of middle powers that includes the likes of Canada, Brazil, and India.

proj-syn.title: What’s Driving Persistent Inflation?
proj-syn.description: In their preoccupation with high public debt, rising bond yields, and dizzying AI valuations, investors have seemingly forgotten the supply shocks shaping the underlying inflation outlook. But anyone worried about debt and yields must reckon with the disruptions created in the name of protecting domestic markets.

proj-syn.title: Building the Economy Africa Needs
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot control global geopolitics, let alone prevent external shocks. But it can manage its exposure, especially by building an integrated continental market, investing in higher-value-added production, and pushing for reform of the global credit-rating agencies.

proj-syn.title: Science Without Scientists?
proj-syn.description: Now that autonomous systems are capable of generating their own hypotheses, designing experiments, and writing up the results, the scientific community must adapt. For scientific knowledge to retain its standing, its sources must be trusted and answerable to the public.

proj-syn.title: When Smart Cities Turn Menacing
proj-syn.description: Uganda has embraced digital-surveillance tools in the name of improving public safety and combating terrorism, a pattern that is repeating itself across several African countries. But governments are increasingly using these technologies for political control, rather than for national security.

proj-syn.title: Brazil Cannot Afford Bolsonaro’s Spending Cuts
proj-syn.description: If he wins the October 25 runoff, far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro plans to slash public spending by as much as 1.5% of GDP. These cuts could push Brazil into recession, hurt workers and small businesses, and drain tax revenue—all without solving the country’s debt problem.

proj-syn.title: A Generational Reckoning on the Streets of Paris
proj-syn.description: As their schools deteriorate and the planet grows hotter, many young people in France do not have hope for a decent future. The recent protests may foreshadow a broader conflict between older generations who wield political power and younger people who must live in the world they leave behind.

proj-syn.title: The Algorithm Driving French Student Protests
proj-syn.description: One of the main drivers of the student protests in France is the opposition to Parcoursup, the country’s university-admissions platform, which is widely denounced as opaque and unfair. While such automated decision-making systems do not create educational inequalities, they can exacerbate them.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives A Varied Lineup Of Large Financings
crunchbase.description: It was another interesting week for AI-related startup funding, with a number of large rounds and quirky companies. The largest financings went to Tenstorrent, a developer of AI processors and systems, and AI lab Flapping Airplanes. The quirkiest round, meanwhile, was undoubtedly a $200 million financing for Warhound, which wants to breed elite military dogs. A number of big rounds in areas including biotech, space tech and physical AI rounded out the list.

crunchbase.title: Protecting Trade Secrets In The Age Of AI
crunchbase.description: AI agents create new trade secret risks by allowing employees to access expertise or inadvertently expose proprietary information through personal devices. In this guest commentary, Seth Kugler, a partner at Grellas Shah LLP, warns companies that they should adopt strict AI policies, restrict data access on unmanaged devices, update confidentiality agreements, and act immediately when misuse is suspected.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Robot Training, Space Lasers And Greener Cement
crunchbase.description: From teaching robots to do everyday household chores to using lasers to track satellites in space, this month's crop of interesting startup deals spans some decidedly different corners of tech.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Slingshot Raises $27M In Seed Funding To Build An Insurer For Those Small Policies Sold At Checkout
crunchbase.description: Slingshot Insurance, a Minneapolis-based AI-native embedded insurance startup, is emerging from stealth with $27 million in a seed funding round co-led by Rally Ventures and Skyward Group, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

crunchbase.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
crunchbase.description: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and measurable customer outcomes rather than expensive models alone.

crunchbase.title: Acquirers Are Snapping Up Boom-Era Startups That Haven’t Raised Funding In Years
crunchbase.description: A number of companies whose names might feature on a playlist of 2021 boom-era unicorns have sold to acquirers in recent months, including one-time highfliers like Airtable, Headspace and Miro. In many cases, companies are selling at valuations which, while not puny, are still far below their former peaks.

crunchbase.title: Your Next Customer Might Be An Agent. Here’s How To Build Your Brand For Both Humans And AI.
crunchbase.description: As AI agents increasingly recommend and purchase products, brands must appeal to both machines and humans by documenting their voice, creating clear product descriptions and checking how AI summarizes their messaging. Guest author Toby Coulthard suggests that startups should build these practices in from the outset, preserving human appeal while measuring success through conversions and revenue rather than content volume.

crunchbase.title: When A Startup Sells, Its Employees’ Equity Plans Can Change Overnight
crunchbase.description: Startup acquisitions can reshape employees’ finances and careers, with individual outcomes depending on a variety of conditions. Guest author Ron Honig, co-CEO and managing partner of From-Honig Family Office, suggests that before making major life changes, employees should clarify their award rights, when proceeds will become available, and what their after-tax payout can realistically support.

crunchbase.title: ‘Weird And Maybe Uninvestable’: How Reach Capital Spots Its Venture Winners
crunchbase.description: Crunchbase News spoke with James Kim, partner at Reach Capital, about how Reach’s education roots inform its broader strategy, what it saw in AI detection company GPTZero, and why some of its best investments initially divided its own team. We also discussed how ownership stakes and secondary transactions have shaped the firm’s approach to returning capital.

crunchbase.title: How To Build A Billion-Dollar Company Without Venture Capital
crunchbase.description: Founders can build billion-dollar businesses without venture capital by prioritizing customer revenue, pricing for quality, hiring exceptional talent and automating processes to scale efficiently, argues Nacho De Marco, who draws on his experience bootstrapping BairesDev, to emphasize financial discipline and a lasting commitment to solving customer problems as the foundations of sustainable growth.
